channel.title: YR Signal — Trade Log, Market Research & Economic Analysis
channel.description: A public trade log, market research, and economic analysis — real moves, real reasoning, no dollar amounts or position sizes.

item.title: Nvidia Beats, and the Whole AI-Infrastructure Complex Exhales
item.description: Nvidia's post-close beat — revenue +106% YoY, data center the bulk of it, next-year guidance well ahead — sent the stock up ~9% and lifted the adjacent networking/power/cooling names that depend on hyperscaler capex. Palo Alto +14% on acquisition-mode reporting plus a strong cybersecurity-peer print. The read-through, not the single stock, is the point.

item.title: Routine Top-Up Into a Broad, Macro-Driven Selloff — One Filled, One Still Queued
item.description: Two routine broad-index top-ups on a session where equities, not just one sector, sold off broadly (S&P 500 -0.83%, Nasdaq-100 -0.72%, Russell 2000 -1.34%) while yields eased — the opposite pattern from Aug 19's chip-specific selloff. One order filled at the close; the other was placed after-hours and is still queued for the next open.

item.title: Diversifying Into a Chip-Sector Selloff, Not Buying the Dip in It
item.description: Added broad-market and international index exposure rather than adding to already-concentrated individual chip names during a session where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.4% — reading the move as rate/valuation-driven, not company-specific.

item.title: New Position Filled: A Cleaner-Valued Entry Into the Memory-Chip Theme
item.description: Watchlist name promoted to a real starter position — top-two global memory maker trading well below the multiple of the more obvious names in the same AI-shortage theme.

item.title: A Long-Overdue Trim, Finally Taken
item.description: Partial profit-take on a position that first crossed +71% back in June and had sat un-acted-on since. No new negative catalyst — a broad chip/cybersecurity-sector selloff on the day just made it a good execution window.

item.title: Same Rate Backdrop, Wider Dispersion Underneath It
item.description: Intraday, not an official close — the rate backdrop didn't move (10-Year still 4.68%, Fed funds flat at 3.63%), but there was real dispersion underneath it: one AI-hardware name jumped over 5% while several others gave back 1-3%, with no single macro headline behind it. No new trades landed this session.

item.title: A Broad Rally With Real Names Behind It — Palantir, Tesla, and a Solar-Facility Headline
item.description: A genuine broad-based rally — S&P 500 +0.7%, Nasdaq-100 close to +1.2% — with real stories behind the leaders: Palantir up nearly 5% on continued Q2 momentum, Tesla up almost 4% on a proposed Texas solar-production facility. A couple of AI-infrastructure names gave back ground with no negative catalyst (one even got a price-target raise the same day), while a large healthcare name declined on an actual catalyst — a new cybersecurity/governance lawsuit plus ongoing Medicare Advantage scrutiny.

item.title: Long Rates Finally Ease Off Their Climb, and Tech Catches the Relief
item.description: Official close — the 10-Year yield eased to 4.68% (down 4bp from the prior print) even as the three-month trend still points up, with the 2-Year easing in step and the Fed funds rate flat. Several of the book's largest technology holdings rallied together, a plausible rate-relief tailwind on top of real stock-specific strength. One session of relief inside a still-rising trend, not a new regime — worth watching whether it holds into next week.

item.title: New Position Filled: Dividend Reinvestment
item.description: A fraction-of-a-share dividend reinvestment — logged for completeness rather than significance.

item.title: New Position Filled: A Routine Broad-Index Top-Up
item.description: Order queued the evening before, just after the prior close, filled at this morning's open — the mechanical, no-thesis-needed core-index leg of the book.

item.title: New Position Filled: Standing Recurring MSFT Buy
item.description: The book's own automatic dollar-cost-average schedule into MSFT, running independently of everything else logged here — not a discretionary call.

item.title: Long Rates Keep Climbing While the Fed Holds Still — and Today's Session Showed Exactly Why That Matters
item.description: Intraday read, not an official close — the 10-Year yield pushed to 4.72% (+0.34pp over three months) while the Fed funds rate held flat, the widening gap the real story for the book's technology-heavy core. Two of the book's largest tech names traded down 2-3% on that rate mechanism, while the clean-energy position bucked the pattern with a double-digit jump on no confirmed news yet. The AI-driven memory-chip shortage theme rallied broadly on the watchlist. What to watch: July's CPI print lands today.

item.title: New Position Filled: A Routine Broad-Index Top-Up
item.description: Order queued the evening before, just after the prior close, filled at this morning's open — the mechanical, no-thesis-needed core-index leg of the book.

item.title: The Three-Name AI-Power Build Is Complete — and a Broad, Unremarkable Red Day Elsewhere
item.description: Intraday read, not an official close — macro backdrop unchanged (Fed funds 3.63%, 10-Year yield 4.63%). The two remaining legs of the three-name AI-power/diversification build started Aug 6 — a healthcare name and a data-center-infrastructure name, both queued as of yesterday — are now confirmed fills, completing the build alongside the nuclear-heavy utility that filled Aug 7. Elsewhere, a broad, unremarkable pullback across several of the book's largest tech names, no single new catalyst behind it; the two newest positions were the standout gainers.

item.title: New Position Filled: A Chipmaker-Agnostic Data-Center Infrastructure Name, Third Leg of the AI-Power Build
item.description: The order queued after Aug 10's close filled at this morning's open — data-center cooling and power delivery, a chipmaker-agnostic way to add more AI-infrastructure exposure. Third and final leg of the planned CEG/UNH/VRT build, filled the same morning as the healthcare leg below.

item.title: New Position Filled: A Healthcare Name, Filling a Long-Flagged Diversification Gap
item.description: The order queued after Aug 10's close filled at this morning's open — fills a long-flagged healthcare gap, no single-name exposure in the space before this. Low correlation to the rest of this AI-heavy book is the point, not a growth story. Second leg of the planned CEG/UNH/VRT build.

item.title: Energy Leads an Otherwise Mixed Tape, and the AI-Power Starter Position Is Now a Confirmed Fill
item.description: Intraday read, not an official close — macro backdrop unchanged (Fed funds 3.63%, 10-Year yield 4.63%). Energy led today's tape, with both energy-major positions up meaningfully since Friday's close, alongside a defense name and a cybersecurity name (now up well over 100% from entry). The AI-power starter position flagged in the last briefing — a nuclear-heavy utility — is now a confirmed fill, not just a queued order; first leg of a planned three-name build, the other two still watchlist-only pending further funding.

item.title: New Position Filled: A Nuclear-Power Utility, the Cheapest Way Into the AI-Power Buildout Theme
item.description: The order queued after Aug 6's close filled at this morning's open — a nuclear-heavy power utility with real current earnings and a multi-year hyperscaler power contract already in place, at the cheapest multiple found among the AI-power/memory-adjacent names researched this week. First leg of a planned build alongside a healthcare name and a data-center-infrastructure name, both still watchlist-only, filling long-flagged gaps in this book.

item.title: New Position: A Nuclear-Power Utility, the Cheapest Way Into the AI-Power Buildout Theme
item.description: Order placed (queued, executes at next open) for a nuclear-heavy power utility — real current earnings and a multi-year hyperscaler power contract already in place, at the cheapest multiple found among the AI-power/memory-adjacent names researched this week. First leg of a planned build alongside a healthcare name and a data-center-infrastructure name, both filling long-flagged gaps in this book.

item.title: A Memory-Chip Supercycle Meets a Stretched Tape — and the Cheapest Way In Isn't the Obvious One
item.description: The 10-Year yield extended its climb to 4.63%, still the dominant force behind today's tech dispersion. Deeper research thread: an AI-driven memory-chip shortage (NAND prices projected up 200%+ YoY) surfaced two richly-valued names that both gave back sharp gains the same session they were flagged, versus a newly-listed memory-maker ADR trading at roughly a third of peers' multiples on the same shortage exposure. A second look went toward AI-power (a nuclear utility with real earnings and a hyperscaler contract) and long-flagged healthcare/data-center-infrastructure gaps. The book's biggest winner is now up over 114% from its original buy — re-flagged again as a trim candidate. SpaceX bounced despite a share-lockup expiring today.

item.title: Rates Climb Past 4.60%, and AMD's Earnings Beat Gets Priced Like a Warning
item.description: The 10-Year Treasury yield climbed to 4.63% (+0.18pp/3mo) and the 2-Year to 4.20% (+0.25pp/3mo) with Fed funds flat — a market-driven repricing, not a policy shift. Growth/tech names sold off with no earnings attached, a pure discount-rate move; AMD beat Q2 estimates outright and still fell nearly 6% on capex-spend concerns, while Arista beat and rallied over 6% the same evening. Gold caught a real flight-to-safety bid (+4.4%). SpaceX's first-ever public earnings beat estimates but the stock kept falling into a share-lockup expiration landing Aug 6.

item.title: The Fed Holds, Then Microsoft and Meta Split the Room — A Two-Session Catch-Up
item.description: Catch-up covering two skipped-post sessions: the Jul 29 FOMC held rates at 3.5-3.75% (5th straight hold, 3 dissents wanting a hike) and Bloom Energy's Q2 beat resolved its trim-vs-hold question. Jul 30: Microsoft beat cleanly (Azure +43%, RPO +84% to $678B) while Meta missed on EPS despite 28% revenue growth — opposite reactions from the same earnings night. Bloom Energy kept running on a fresh AI-power deal, broad chip/hardware names rallied alongside Microsoft's beat, and the VIX fell sharply confirming a genuine risk-on session.

item.title: Coca-Cola Hits a Record High While Chip Names Keep Sliding — Same Split, Different Day
item.description: Coca-Cola beat on both lines and raised full-year guidance, jumping ~7% to a fresh 52-week high, while AMD (-3.4%), Dell (-9%, despite not reporting until September), and Palantir (-6%) kept sliding on AI-capex/export-restriction fears and a same-day Japan/Korea semiconductor rout. Despite the chip-sector stress, the VIX actually fell — a sign of sector rotation, not broad risk-off, heading into tomorrow's FOMC decision and MSFT/META earnings.

item.title: A China Lithography Breakthrough Crashes Chip Stocks While Oil Crashes for a Different Reason Entirely
item.description: A report that a Shanghai state-backed firm has begun mass-producing homegrown DUV lithography equipment triggered a broad chip-sector selloff (AMD -7.5%, Teradyne -6.1%, Nvidia -5.1%, SMH -3.7%, Micron -4.5% on a second catalyst from a Chinese memory maker's 500%+ Shanghai IPO debut), while crude oil crashed 5-6% on a reported US-Iran weekend strike pause. Money rotated into defense, megacap tech, and defensives instead — RTX, Microsoft, Coca-Cola, Alphabet, and Palantir all gained.

item.title: A Weekend Follow-Up Changes the Story on One Name Ahead of the Busiest Earnings Week of the Summer
item.description: A weekend news check found Bloom Energy's overhang has escalated from a valuation debate into a short-seller report now under a securities class-action investigation — a materially different risk than earlier this week's framing. That lands right as the heaviest earnings week of the summer arrives on top of a Treasury yield four sessions into a climb.

item.title: Not All Red Days Are the Same Story: An Earnings Miss, a Valuation Call, and Plain Momentum
item.description: Tesla's slide is a confirmed earnings miss (margin and free-cash-flow pressure from AI/robotics capex), Bloom Energy's continued decline reads as a valuation debate ahead of its Jul 28 report, and Apple's gain is plain momentum with no single catalyst — three different reasons to move that would look identical on a one-day chart.

item.title: Earnings Season Arrives While the Rate Backdrop Sits Quiet
item.description: The macro calendar is quiet — Fed funds unchanged at 3.63%, the 10-Year near 4.60%, unemployment flat at 4.20%. The bigger driver today is corporate: two mega-cap names report after today's close, the first live earnings test of the season for a Technology-heavy allocation, with two defense names following before tomorrow's open.

item.title: A Flat Headline Hides a Wide Split — And Two Big Earnings Land After the Bell
item.description: A roughly flat index-level day masked real dispersion: a leading server maker jumped nearly 10% on continued AI-infrastructure-demand confirmation, while two mega-cap software names extended pre-earnings drawdowns. A search-and-cloud giant and an EV/energy-storage name both report after today's close — the first live earnings test of the season for this book.

item.title: The Chip Bear Market Reverses Hard on a New Supply Deal and a Bullish Pricing Call
item.description: Four days after the SOX confirmed a bear market, semiconductors staged one of their sharpest reversals of the summer on a new GPU-designer/cloud-provider supply deal plus a bullish sell-side call on memory pricing. A fuel-cell name caught between a bullish infrastructure deal and short-seller allegations finally got a decisive, one-sided catalyst: a major bank price-target hike sent it up double digits.

item.title: Semiconductors Confirm a Bear Market — And Wall Street Is Already Calling the Bottom
item.description: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) has formally entered a bear market, down roughly 20% from its late-June record. Several sell-side banks — Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Mizuho — are already calling the pullback a buying opportunity rather than a fundamentals break, and NVDA/AMD ticked higher on the day. The disagreement isn't whether AI infrastructure spending continues, it's whether the returns show up fast enough to justify current multiples.

item.title: Bloom Energy's $25B Brookfield Deal Collides With Short-Seller Allegations, While SpaceX Nurses a Starship Setback
item.description: Bloom Energy fell despite Brookfield expanding its AI-infrastructure partnership fivefold to $25B, weighed down by two unresolved short-seller reports alleging undisclosed China supply-chain exposure. SpaceX sits roughly 45% off its post-IPO high after an aborted Starship test flight, with the next attempt rescheduled for Thursday, Jul 23.

item.title: Semiconductors Post Their Worst Week Since Last Spring on AI-Capex Doubts
item.description: A broad, sector-wide selloff hit semiconductors today — down roughly 20% from their recent record on doubts the AI-capex spending spree can keep justifying itself, sharpened by a competitive new open-weight model from a Chinese AI startup. Energy, cybersecurity, and gold held up; the real test is whether Big Tech trims capex guidance at earnings over the next two weeks.

item.title: Buy: XLU (Starter)
item.description: New utilities-sector position — filling a real, long-flagged gap in the book. AI power-demand is a genuine secular tailwind, not just a defensive filler pick. Picked over a real-estate ETF I'd also been considering for the same slot — that one hit a fresh 52-week high the same day this went in.

item.title: Buy: VXUS (Starter)
item.description: New international-diversification position — zero non-US exposure was a real, repeatedly-flagged gap. Chosen over a REIT ETF alternative for the same new-money slot: starting from literally zero international exposure won out over a smaller tax optimization.

item.title: Buy: GOOGL (Building)
item.description: Continued build — still working toward a full-size position. Sized down from an originally larger planned add after deciding to hold back part of this round's new money for a near-term cash need.

item.title: Buy: MSFT (Core)
item.description: Continued DCA into one of the book's most underwater quality holdings, ahead of the late-July earnings window. Sized down from an originally larger planned add for the same reason as today's GOOGL add.

item.title: Market Notes: A Rotation Inside Tech — AI-Hardware Sells Off While Mega-Cap Software Rallies
item.description: No new Fed/Treasury data today, so the session's moves came from company news, not a rate signal. A major hardware name fell double digits on reports a large social-media company may lease out surplus AI compute — raising hyperscaler-overbuild concerns — plus memory-cost margin pressure and a valuation downgrade. A leading memory-chip maker dropped nearly 8% on Chinese DRAM competition and possible export-control tightening, dragging the broader chip complex with it. Meanwhile mega-cap software (search/cloud, consumer electronics, enterprise software, e-commerce) rallied together, and the largest AI-chip designer held here sat out both stories, essentially flat. Reads as a rotation within tech, not a broad move.

item.title: Market Notes: Cool CPI Flips Yesterday's Rotation — Growth Rallies, Energy Cools Off
item.description: June CPI fell -0.4% month-over-month, the largest single-month drop since April 2020, on a sharp energy-index decline — core CPI held near +2.85% YoY. Markets flipped Monday's rotation: semiconductor and AI-infrastructure names rallied 3-4% together, a defense-AI software name's rally has now pushed it above its own average analyst target, and a hardware name jumped hardest on AI-server-backlog reports plus a software-to-hardware divergence trade after a peer's revenue warning. Yesterday's winners — energy majors and defensives — cooled off in the mirror image. One data point doesn't reverse a policy stance; the July 28-29 FOMC is the real test.

item.title: Market Notes: A Clean Rotation Day — AI/Growth Sells Off, Energy and Mega-Cap Software Catch a Bid
item.description: Monday mirrored the Jul 2 rotation, playing out inside the existing rate backdrop with no new FRED data behind it. Semiconductor and AI-power names fell 3-5% together, a fuel-cell name still working through last week's short-seller story gave up similar ground, and a newly-public space-launch name kept sliding — while energy majors caught a bid on the cracked Iran ceasefire and mega-cap cloud software was one of the few green names in tech. Correlated moves across a whole sector on a no-data day read as rotation, not a verdict on any one name — Tuesday's CPI print is the real test.

item.title: Market Notes: A Short-Seller Report Gets a Formal Rebuttal, and the Week Ahead Has Three Real Catalysts
item.description: Bloom Energy filed a formal SEC 8-K on Jul 9 rebutting last week's short-seller report point by point — a stronger response than a press denial, though still unconfirmed by any third party. Looking ahead: June CPI lands Tuesday (nowcast ~3.96% YoY), big-bank earnings kick off the same morning, and futures-implied Fed hike odds have moved further hawkish this week specifically (July FOMC 31%, up from 17%; September 84%, up from 61%).

item.title: Market Notes: A Weekend Gut-Check — Which Drawdowns Are Real, and Which Are Just Cost-Basis Math
item.description: A weekend review of five long-underwater names found two very different stories. Gold, two energy majors, a defense name, and a mega-cap tech name are all down mostly on entry-timing (bought near local tops before pullbacks that have since started reversing), with the underlying thesis for each intact. A newly-public space-launch company down over 20% is different — a large bond offering, a still-rich ~100x-sales valuation, and creeping share-lockup expirations are real, unresolved risk, not market overreaction. Takeaway: "down a lot" and "thesis broken" are different claims, and conflating them either way is a mistake.

item.title: Market Notes: Two Different Kinds of "AI Stock Down" — And Why They're Not the Same Risk
item.description: Three AI-adjacent names moved sharply today for three different reasons: Meta jumped ~6% on a genuinely new cloud-compute business launch and in-house AI chip news; Bloom Energy fell ~6% on a short-seller report alleging misleading supply-chain disclosures (denied by management); Palo Alto Networks fell ~4% on hawkish-Fed valuation compression alone. "AI stocks were mixed" is true but low-information — a demand re-rating, a credibility dispute, and a rate-driven multiple compression are three distinct risks that happened to land on the same day.

item.title: Market Notes: The Fed's Hawkish Pivot — Why "No Rate Cut" Wasn't the Real Story
item.description: The Fed held rates steady June 17, but the dot plot flipped hawkish — 9 of 18 officials now project a hike by year-end under new Chair Kevin Warsh, with October hike odds now being priced. That reverses the cut-leaning backdrop most of H1 was priced against, and raises the bar for paying up on long-duration growth names that already re-rated higher since June, versus sectors with steadier demand or a direct AI-infrastructure angle (utilities, energy, industrials).

item.title: Market Notes: The Chip Sleeve Bounces Back
item.description: Two sessions after the Samsung-earnings/DeepSeek selloff hit semiconductor and AI-adjacent names, most of that move is reversing — the same names leading the decline are leading the bounce back, with no new catalyst behind it beyond the initial scare fading. Read as a headline-driven round-trip rather than a fundamentals shift in either direction; the real signal is whether these names hold the bounce through the next earnings cycle or keep whipsawing on every AI-competition headline.

item.title: Market Notes: A Chip-Specific Selloff, Not a Broad One
item.description: Samsung's soft quarterly results plus a Reuters report that China's DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip triggered a sharp semiconductor selloff — a popular chip ETF fell ~4.5% while the Nasdaq was down only ~0.6% and the S&P 500 ~0.2%. Nvidia itself was little changed to higher, suggesting the market is treating this as a competitive/supply-chain story rather than a broad AI-trade reversal. Worth tracking as a distinct risk from this year's rate-driven rotations.

item.title: Market Notes: Records and a Rotation, Heading Into the Holiday Weekend
item.description: The last session before the July 4th break produced a genuinely odd pairing: the Dow closed at a fresh record — its fourth straight — while the Nasdaq fell for a second consecutive day, on a soft June jobs report (57K vs. ~113K est.) that lowered near-term Fed hike odds. Chips fell for a second straight session (~12% over two days), Tesla dropped ~7% despite beating delivery estimates, and Europe/Japan were mixed. Watch into the Jul 6 reopen: chip stabilization and a tariff court appeal.

item.title: Buy: RTX · GOOGL (Building / Core)
item.description: Leaning into the sector rotation playing out this week — money moving out of tech/semis (up 80%+ in H1) into industrials and defense. RTX gets the bigger add: a fresh $1.1B Navy missile contract, raised full-year guidance, and an analyst upgrade to Buy. GOOGL gets a smaller top-up given rising capex guidance has compressed near-term free cash flow margin ahead of earnings. Queued — fills Mon Jul 6 (market closed Jul 3 for the holiday).

item.title: Buy: META (Core)
item.description: Topping up my most underwater quality holding after a sharp single-day pullback — same ad-monetization + AI thesis as the Jun 23 add, just a cheaper entry. Queued — fills Mon Jul 6 (market closed Jul 3 for the holiday).

item.title: Buy: VTI · VOO (Core)
item.description: Routine systematic index contribution — no new thesis here, just staying consistent with regular broad-market buying regardless of what else is happening that week. Queued — fills Mon Jul 6 (market closed Jul 3 for the holiday).

item.title: Market Notes: A Clean Rotation Day
item.description: A textbook rotation session, not a broad selloff — TSLA, DELL, BE, META, AMD, ANET, NVDA sold off while AAPL, LMT, RTX, KO, XLV, and GLD rallied together. Reads as profit-taking funding a rotation, not a thesis break for the names that sold off.

item.title: Market Notes: H1 2026 Sector Rotation — What Actually Moved
item.description: Tech (XLK) led H1 2026 up ~25%, but Energy (+16.6%) and Industrials (+16.4%) nearly matched it — industrials increasingly a second-order AI-infrastructure play via power, cooling, and physical buildout. Consumer Discretionary was the lone red sector, down ~1%.

item.title: Market Notes: The 2s10s Curve and What It's Telling Us
item.description: The 2-Year Treasury yield has climbed faster than the 10-Year through H1 2026 — a flattening move that signals the market pricing in less near-term Fed easing, not tighter policy. Long-duration, high-multiple growth names are the most exposed to this kind of repricing.

item.title: Buy: GOOGL (Building)
item.description: New position — the last Mag7 name I didn't hold. Cloud growing ~63% YoY, reasonable multiple for the growth rate, and Gemini is showing up in the numbers, not just the keynote. Building this slowly over a few months rather than going in all at once.

item.title: Sell: WMT · F · QQQ · SMH
item.description: Cleaned out four small, low-conviction positions I'd accumulated without a real thesis behind any of them. Redeployed straight into names I actually wanted to be bigger in (MSFT/META), same day.

item.title: Buy: MSFT · META (Core)
item.description: Adding to my two most underwater quality holdings ahead of their late-July earnings. Both pulled back hard on broad tech weakness this year with no change to the underlying growth story — Azure and AI ad-load are still doing the work.

item.title: Buy: PLTR (Starter)
item.description: New position. Federal AI/data contracts (Army, and increasingly defense-adjacent "Golden Dome" work) are becoming a real revenue line, not just a narrative. Starting small.

item.title: Buy: RTX (Starter)
item.description: New defense position. Missile/interceptor demand tied to the same Golden Dome buildout as PLTR — pairing a hardware prime with a software integrator.

item.title: Sell: AAPL · META
item.description: Small rebalance in a satellite account, same cleanup day as the WMT/F/QQQ/SMH sells — trimming a couple of tiny, low-conviction odd-lot positions to concentrate further into the names getting added that day.

item.title: Trim: BE
item.description: Partial trim after a sharp one-day drop tied to a competitor (fuel cells) losing out on a gas-turbine deal, plus some insider selling. Kept half the position — the AI-power-demand thesis isn't broken, but the news changed my sizing, not my direction.

item.title: Buy: XLV (Starter)
item.description: New healthcare sector position — this was a real gap in the book. Low correlation to the AI trade, defensive characteristics, decent momentum in 2026.

item.title: Market Notes: AI's Power Bottleneck — Why Compute Isn't the Constraint Anymore
item.description: The AI buildout narrative has shifted from compute scarcity to power availability — data center demand is projected to keep climbing sharply through 2030. The trade is no longer just semis and hyperscalers, it's the power producers and grid-adjacent names behind them.

item.title: Trim: PANW · GLD · AMD
item.description: Locking in some gains across three big winners in one session — PANW and AMD were both up well over 50% from cost, GLD had run hard too. Kept the core of each; this was profit-taking, not an exit.

item.title: Sell: AMC
item.description: Full exit on a legacy meme-stock position from years ago. No fundamental thesis was ever attached to this one — just cleaning it out.

item.title: Buy: JPM (Starter)
item.description: New financials position — another sector gap. Steeper yield curve and an active M&A environment both favor big banks here.

item.title: Buy: DELL (Building)
item.description: AI infrastructure hardware exposure alongside NVDA/AMD — a different part of the same buildout (servers, not just chips).

item.title: Buy: TSLA · BE · AMD (Core)
item.description: Adds across existing positions on a pullback — no new thesis, just buying more of what I already believed in at a better price.

item.title: Buy: CVX · XOM (Core)
item.description: Built out a dual-major energy position (both CVX and XOM, deliberately, not either/or). Straightforward hedge against oil-price and inflation surprises the rest of the book doesn't cover.

item.title: Buy: LMT · PANW (Building)
item.description: Defense budget tailwinds (LMT) and continued conviction in the security name ahead of what turned into a big run (PANW).

item.title: Buy: GLD (Core)
item.description: Building a gold hedge in three tranches. Simple macro hedge against real-rate surprises and dollar weakness — not a trade on gold going up, a hedge for if everything else goes down.

item.title: Buy: ANET (Starter)
item.description: Networking hardware for AI data centers — same buildout as DELL/NVDA, different layer of the stack.
